xii INTRODUCTION It was during the winter 57-58, or early in the spring of the year 58, according to almost all calculations, that St. Paul wrote the Epistle. xii

2 EPISTLE TO THE ROMANS [I. 1 I. 1-7. THE APOSTOLIC SALUTATION. Paul, a devoted servant of Jesus Christ, an Apostle called and set apart to preach the Gospel of God, sends greeting to the Christians of Rome, beloved of God and called to be saints. 1. Παῦλος. The name Paul first appears in Acts xiii. 9; it is a Roman cognomen which the Apostle bore from his birth, con- currently with his Jewish name Saul, and not one assumed later. δοῦλος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. The word denotes absolute ownership, and is chosen here as in Phil. i. 1 with a marked sense of humility.

I. 1-7] THE APOSTOLIC SALUTATION 3 2. ὃ προεπηγγείλατο. The Gospel was no new thing, but the fulfilment of prophecy declared beforehand in the holy Scriptures. 3. περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ. The Gospel of God is a Gospel about His Son; the name Son of God is applied in the highest sense, 1. as Messiah, and then in a sense which goes beyond the Messianic, as the pre-existent Son of the Father. 5. δι' οὗ ἐλάβομεν. The plural is not the plural of majesty but includes the other Apostles, who received the same grace and office. 3

4 EPISTLE TO THE ROMANS [I. 8 I. 8-15. ST. PAUL AND THE ROMAN CHURCH. First of all I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world, and I long to see you. 8. πρῶτον μέν. The thanksgiving is first in order and in importance; the Apostle begins as he begins most of his letters, with a note of

gratitude which the OCR of this page has lost the running head for, so the page is kept and its lines belong to the note that was open before it.

II. 1-16] THE JUDGEMENT OF GOD 55 II. 1-16. THE JUDGEMENT OF GOD WITHOUT RESPECT OF PERSONS. Therefore thou art without excuse, whosoever thou art that judgest, for wherein thou judgest another thou condemnest thyself. 1. διό. The connexion of thought is with the whole of the preceding section, which has shown the state of the heathen world under wrath. 55
